name: Abishag
overview: Abishag was a female figure known as the Shunammite and served as David's nurse, as recorded in 1 Kings 1:3-4. The Scripture does not specify her tribal affiliation or additional personal details. Her role was significant in the care of King David during his old age.
namesAndTitles: The name Abishag means '[my] father strays,' as noted in 1 Kings 1:3. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God, and no further titles are recorded for her.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Abishag beyond her role as David's nurse. There are no additional relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abishag's importance lies in her service to King David in his later years, providing care and companionship during a time of physical weakness. Her presence highlights the human vulnerability of the king and the faithful service rendered to him. Though not a central figure, her role contributes to the narrative surrounding David's final days.
